title: Choose GitDonkey's visual world
question: The roll assigned Patch Bay. Keep it, take an alternate, or re-roll.

options.label: Patch Bay
options.lineage: Eurorack modular synthesizers: anodized panels, screen-printed legends, patch cables
options.thesis: Your repo as a patched modular rig: branches are coloured cables, commits are jacks, merging is patching one cable into another.
options.viewport: Matte black rig: tabs as a rail, toolbar as a row of keyed modules with legends, sidebar a jack field, the graph's lanes drawn as cables with a hint of sag, the commit panel a module with LED state.
options.risk: Tips into skeuomorphic gear-porn if knobs, screws and textures creep in; the panels must stay flat and typographic.

raised.raise: Hairline module grid: panels tile edge to edge on 1px seams with no padding inflation, so a 28px commit row holds five columns cleanly.
No easing curves: every state change is a crisp switch-throw under 120ms, and elevation exists only as panel ply, never as glow.
Stamped codes: every commit carries its short SHA as a printed code, and selection is a ring around the jack, not a filled row.
Hierarchy by scale and weight alone: legends carry no ornament, no icon tiles, no gradients.

options.label: Transit Diagram
options.lineage: Vignelli's 1972 New York subway diagram and Beck's Tube map
options.thesis: History drawn as a transit diagram: branches are lines, commits are stations, merges are interchanges.
options.viewport: Charcoal shell; the graph is the hero, drawn with 45° line turns and station dots; the current branch's line is labelled like a route bullet in the toolbar.
options.risk: The most familiar reading: git-as-subway-map is the stock metaphor and GitKraken's graph already reads this way.

options.label: Concourse Wayfinding
options.thesis: Every repo state signed like a concourse junction: where you are, where you can go, and how far.
options.viewport: Black shell with one yellow band naming the current branch and its distance from upstream (↑2 ↓1) at monumental scale; yellow appears nowhere else.
options.case: Fuses well: current branch and upstream distance map to gate and walking minutes. Holds product clarity, loses audience identification to the patch bay.
options.risk: A yellow band all day can fatigue; the discipline only works if yellow stays reserved for 'you are here'.

options.label: Orienteering Course
options.lineage: ISOM orienteering maps and control legends
options.thesis: History as terrain in a fixed ink language, with your branch's path riding above it in one course colour.
options.viewport: The graph as muted terrain; HEAD's first-parent lineage drawn in course purple with numbered control circles; a legend table in the side panel.
options.case: Fuses cleanly: HEAD's lineage becomes the course. Holds product clarity, loses audience identification.
options.risk: Muted terrain can make every other branch too quiet to read at a glance.

options.label: High-Density Module Web
options.thesis: Every repo fact packed into hairline-ruled modules with small red tabs.
options.viewport: A mosaic of ruled modules: branches, files, commits all tiled edge to edge.
options.case: Fuses poorly: a mixed-skill team drowns in the density, and the white ground fights the dark-mode requirement.
options.kept: Kept its hairline module grid with no padding inflation.
options.risk: Clutter for anyone who isn't already an expert.

options.label: Acetate Tab Manual
options.lineage: Boxed-software reference manuals with acetate overlays
options.thesis: Each section a coloured divider board with clear acetate leaves above it.
options.viewport: Graph, changes and commit as tabbed divider sections down the fore edge.
options.case: Fuses poorly: a reading-measure book form slows an all-day operating tool.
options.kept: Kept its stepped, easing-free motion and ply-only elevation.
options.risk: Reads as a book, not a tool.

options.label: Convention Circle Catalog
options.thesis: Commits as stamp-sized cells in a numbered hall grid.
options.viewport: A dense numbered grid of commit cells keyed to a branch map.
options.case: Fuses poorly: a grid loses the parent/child topology the graph exists to show.
options.kept: Kept its stamped codes and ring-not-fill selection.

options.label: Variable Type Specimen
options.thesis: Hierarchy by type scale alone, driven live by sliders.
options.viewport: One giant glyph-scale statement with tiny utility labels.
options.case: Fuses poorly: nothing in daily Git work maps to an axis slider.
options.kept: Kept hierarchy by scale and weight alone, with no ornament.
options.risk: Pure typography leaves the graph without a material language.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: GitKraken's world played straight: slate-dark shell, teal accent, avatar-node graph.
canonCard.viewport: The three-pane GitKraken arrangement at full craft.
